Lake District: The Scenic Motorcycle Guide

The Lake District packs extraordinary riding into a compact area. Within 30 miles in any direction from Keswick, you can ride England's steepest passes, circuit its most beautiful lakes, and blast across open fells. Here's the definitive guide to the best roads.

The Must-Ride Passes

  • Hardknott Pass: England's steepest road at 33% gradient. Tight hairpins, vertiginous drops, Roman fort at the summit. Not for beginners or heavy touring bikes.
  • Wrynose Pass: Hardknott's slightly gentler partner. Usually ridden in combination for the full lakeland pass experience.
  • Honister Pass: Between Borrowdale and Buttermere. Steep but wider than Hardknott. The slate mine adds industrial heritage to the mountain drama.
  • Kirkstone Pass: The highest pass in the Lakes on a main road. The Kirkstone Pass Inn at the summit is one of England's highest pubs.
  • Newlands Pass: A gentle, flowing pass between Buttermere and Braithwaite. Beautiful in a softer way than the dramatic passes.

Best Lake Shore Roads

  • Ullswater (A592): The most beautiful lake road in England. The east shore between Glenridding and Pooley Bridge is consistently stunning.
  • Buttermere (B5289): A compact, gorgeous loop with mountain scenery reflected in still water.
  • Wastwater: England's deepest lake in its most dramatic setting. The road along the north shore beneath the Screes is extraordinary.

Quiet Alternative Roads

  • Ennerdale: No through road, but the ride to the road end at Ennerdale Water is peaceful and beautiful.
  • Eskdale: The valley between Hardknott and the coast. The narrow road through Eskdale is quiet and charming.
  • Duddon Valley: Wordsworth's favourite valley. The road follows the River Duddon through ancient woodland.
The Lake District's biggest challenge is traffic. Summer weekends and school holidays bring heavy congestion to the A591, A66, and main village centres. The solution: ride early, ride midweek, or ride the lesser-known valleys. The quiet roads are often the most beautiful.

Best Times to Ride

  • May-June: Long days, lambs in the fields, wildflowers. Roads are quieter than summer.
  • September-October: Autumn colours are magnificent. Bracken turns gold and the oak woods glow amber.
  • Early morning (any season): Before 9am, even summer roads are quiet. The light on the fells at dawn is extraordinary.

Local Knowledge and Tips

The Lake District is remarkably compact — no point is more than 30 miles from another within the national park boundary. This means you can easily change plans mid-ride if weather deterioration or unexpected traffic makes one route less appealing than another. Local knowledge suggests riding the western fells for solitude, the central fells for drama, and the eastern fells for the best road surfaces and flowing riding character.

Hawkshead, Coniston, and Boot are charming villages that see significantly less tourist traffic than the main centres of Keswick, Windermere, and Ambleside. For excellent food and drink, the Drunken Duck Inn near Ambleside serves its own brewery ales alongside superb food in a historic setting. The Borrowdale Gates Hotel is a popular biker stop with panoramic views across Derwentwater and secure motorcycle parking. If persistent rain arrives, the Pencil Museum in Keswick and the Wordsworth Museum in Grasmere are atmospheric wet-weather diversions that keep you entertained until the skies clear. faq.q: Is Hardknott Pass suitable for a large touring bike?
faq.a: Hardknott Pass is England's steepest road at up to 33 percent, with tight hairpins, vertiginous drops and a frequently wet surface. It is not recommended for beginners or heavy, fully loaded touring bikes. You must be confident with hill starts on extreme gradients and prepared for oncoming traffic on blind bends. If in doubt, the wider Honister or Kirkstone passes give mountain drama with less risk.

faq.q: Which is the best lake road to ride?
faq.a: The A592 along Ullswater's east shore, between Glenridding and Pooley Bridge, is widely considered the most beautiful lake road in England and is consistently stunning. Aira Force waterfall is on the route and the view from Hallin Fell car park across the lake is superb. For raw drama, the Wastwater road beneath the Screes is extraordinary but far quieter.

faq.q: How do I avoid the worst of the traffic?
faq.a: Traffic is the Lake District's biggest challenge, with summer weekends and school holidays clogging the A591, A66 and main villages. The solution is to ride early, ideally before 9am when even summer roads are quiet, or ride midweek and in the shoulder season. Choosing lesser-known valleys such as Eskdale, Ennerdale and the Duddon avoids the crowds and often the most beautiful scenery.

faq.q: When is the best time to ride the Lakes?
faq.a: May and June bring long days, lambs and wildflowers with quieter roads than high summer. September and October deliver magnificent autumn colours as bracken turns gold and the oak woods glow amber. Early morning in any season is best of all, with quiet roads and extraordinary light on the fells at dawn. Avoid peak summer weekends where you can.
